Amy is baking a loaf of bread. If the loaf weighs [MATH: 12] ounces, then Amy needs to bake the loaf for [MATH: 40] minutes. There is a proportional relationship between the loaf's weight (in ounces) and the time (in minutes) the loaf needs to bake.

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: x] be the loaf's weight (in ounces), and [MATH: y] be the time (in minutes) the loaf needs to bake.

First, we need to construct the equation that represents the proportional relationship. Every proportional relationship takes the form [MATH: y=kx,] where [MATH: k] is the constant of proportionality.

We are told that if the loaf weighs [MATH: x=12] ounces, then Amy needs to bake it for [MATH: y=40] minutes. We can find the constant of proportionality by computing the ratio of the [MATH: y]-value to the [MATH: x]-value, as follows:

[MATH: k = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{40}{12} = \dfrac{40 \div 4}{12 \div 4} = \dfrac{10}{3}]

Therefore, the equation is

[MATH: y = \dfrac{10}{3} x.]

Now, we want to find the value of [MATH: x] so that the loaf will bake for exactly [MATH: y=60] minutes. So, we substitute [MATH: y=60] into the equation above:

[MATH: 60|= (10)/(3)x; (10)/(3)x|= 60]

To solve for [MATH: x,] we multiply both sides of the equation by the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{10}{3},] which is [MATH: \dfrac{3}{10}.] We get

[MATH: (3)/(10) × (10)/(3)x|= (3)/(10) × 60; 1x|= (3 × 60)/(10); x|= (180)/(10); x|= 18.]

Therefore, the loaf of bread should weigh [MATH: 18] ounces.
